To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) interpolated faces cause impairment in memories for related target face, (2) the impairment effects disappear after 2 days, (3) the impairment and recovery effects occur regardless of participants' beliefs about whether the interpolated faces were the same or similar to the targets, and (4) these effects suggest that the retrieval, not storage, of target memories is impaired by interpolated faces.
interpolated faces cause impairment effects on recognition memory for related target faces, and that this impairment effect is eliminated after 48 hr.

interpolated faces cause impairment effects that can be recovered after a delay, and that the recovery effects occur even if participants are successfully misled about the nature of the interpolated faces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the impairment effect and the conditions under which it is likely to occur.
the nature of the retrieval-based impairment effects and the role of beliefs in memory.
the nature of memory impairment caused by interpolated faces and the role of participants' beliefs in the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
interpolated faces can impair memories for related target stimuli, but that the effect is not necessarily permanent.
interpolated faces can cause retrieval-based impairment to memories for target faces.
interpolated faces cause impairment and that this impairment is based on retrieval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
retrieval-based impairment can occur for faces, and it is not moderated by participants belief about the interpolated faces.
retrieval-based impairment is a robust effect that is independent of the participants' beliefs about whether the interpolated faces were similar or different from the targets.
the effects of interpolated faces are retrieval-based.
The main takeaway from our work is that
retrieval-based impairment effects can be obtained in the face domain and that the effects of interpolated stimuli can be recovered after 48 hr.
memory impairment can result from retrieval interference, even when participants are not aware of the interference.
memory for faces can be impaired by interpolated faces even when the faces are presented in a different context.
